title: Game of Life
statement_short: Given an m x n grid of cells, each live or dead, update the board to its next state according to Conway's Game of Life rules, where transitions happen simultaneously.
constraints: m == board.length, n == board[i].length, 1 <= m, n <= 25, board[i][j] is 0 or 1
hint: Simultaneous cell transitions require encoding the next state alongside the current state in-place using bit flags.
keywords: update the board to its next state
why_not: Right: Bit Manipulation uses 2-bit state encoding (or state flags) to compute simultaneous cell transitions in-place in O(m \* n) time and O(1) space. Not 2D DP: Subproblem state caching is unnecessary when board transitions depend only on immediate 8-neighbor counts. Not Graph BFS: Queue traversal is unneeded because all grid cells are updated simultaneously. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Storing modified cell coordinates uses O(m \* n) extra memory instead of in-place bit manipulation.
